game_20260219_091818_g8:49.description: Death's Shadow was cast when Kimi25 Diplom's life total was too high for it to survive. Death's Shadow is a 13/13 that gets -X/-X where X is your life total. Starting at 20, losing 1 (Bloodstained Mire) and 2 (Watery Grave) puts them at 17 life, making Death's Shadow a 13-17 = -4/-4, which means it dies immediately as a state-based action (0 or less toughness). This wastes the card entirely for no benefit.

game_20260226_003306_g4:3.description: Bottomed Hollow One, which is the primary payoff for the Burning Inquiry discard synergy. With Burning Inquiry in hand, Turn 1 Mountain → Burning Inquiry → free Hollow One (4/4) is the explosive line this deck is built around. Discarding 3 cards from Burning Inquiry reduces Hollow One's cost by 6, making it free.

game_20260217_223017_g8:24.description: Kimi25 Snark incorrectly evaluated their mana and believed they couldn't cast Shoot the Sheriff or Tishana's Tidebinder, when both were castable. Watery Grave produces {B}, enabling Shoot the Sheriff ({1}{B}) to destroy the opponent's Oblivious Bookworm before it starts generating card advantage at end step.

game_20260219_091818_g8:72.description: Death's Shadow was cast at too high a life total (around 17 life), causing it to immediately die as a state-based action (-4/-4 or worse). This wastes one of the deck's primary win conditions for absolutely no value.

game_20260226_003306_g4:6.description: Chose Walking Ballista over Eldrazi Temple from the Devourer of Destiny reveal. The hand contains expensive cards (Devourer of Destiny at 7 mana, Kozilek's Command with X cost, Glaring Fleshraker at 3) and only 4 lands (Forest, Eldrazi Temple, Ugin's Labyrinth, Boseiju). A second Eldrazi Temple would provide significant mana acceleration for Eldrazi spells, potentially enabling a turn 3-4 Devourer of Destiny or a large Kozilek's Command much earlier.

game_20260226_003306_g4:32.description: Playing Mountain instead of Bloodstained Mire. Generally in Modern, you want to deploy fetch lands early for deck thinning and flexibility, saving basics for later. With Burning Inquiry in hand that could randomly discard the Mire, deploying it now is slightly better. The fetch could also find a Swamp later if needed for Street Wraith's BB cost.

game_20260226_003306_g4:22.description: Fetched Blood Crypt instead of a basic Mountain, paying 2 unnecessary life. The player already has an untapped Blood Crypt on the battlefield for black mana, so they can cast Orcish Bowmasters ({1}{B}) with existing Blood Crypt (B) + any untapped land (1). A basic Mountain entering untapped for free accomplishes the same thing.

game_20260219_091818_g6:43.description: Cast Young Wolf before playing a land drop this turn. With Wooded Foothills and Forest in hand, they need to play a land to develop toward casting Yawgmoth (4 mana) next turn. If the turn ended after Young Wolf without a land drop, that's a missed land drop. Even if they could still play a land, casting the spell first before playing the land is poor sequencing - play lands before spells when possible.

game_20260226_003306_g4:9.description: Playing Blood Crypt (likely paying 2 life to enter untapped) when Mountain would have provided the same R mana this turn for free. The player only needs R mana on turn 2 for Marauding Mako or Burning Inquiry. Black mana isn't needed until turn 3 at earliest (for Orcish Bowmasters), so saving Blood Crypt for later preserves options at no cost.

game_20260226_003306_g4:14.description: Played Boseiju, Who Endures instead of Eldrazi Temple. Eldrazi Temple would provide CC for Eldrazi spells, which is critically important for this Eldrazi deck. With Ugin's Labyrinth (CC) + Eldrazi Temple (CC for Eldrazi), the player would have 4 mana available for Eldrazi spells, enabling Glaring Fleshraker (3 mana) this turn with mana to spare, and better setting up future turns for Kozilek's Command. Boseiju's green mana and channel ability are largely irrelevant in this board state compared to Eldrazi Temple's acceleration.
